cohort: The study cohort included 360 women with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and 1440 matched control women with subsequent singleton pregnancies in Helsinki University Hospital, Finland, between 2007 and 2016.
finding: Women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss had a significantly higher risk for gestational hypertension, preterm birth, malpresentation, premature rupture of membranes, lower mean birthweight, and higher risk of umbilical artery pH <7.10 in their subsequent pregnancies compared to controls.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was comparable between RPL women and controls, though RPL women had a higher incidence of induced labor.
birth_weight: Cases: 3387 g (± 680 g), Controls: 3482 g (± 564 g)
